title: Does short-selling threat discipline managers in mergers and acquisitions decisions?

rival_explanations: institutional investors identify good (value-enhancing) managers and also lend out shares, so LS reflects manager quality rather than a short-selling governance threat
supply-side information: passive lenders (index funds/ETFs) increase lending supply when they expect the manager to make good M&A decisions

mechanism.hypothesis: likelihood of being an acquiring firm

context.industry_setting: cross-industry (U.S. domestic M&A across two-digit / Fama-French five industries; no focal sector)
context.sample_description: Completed U.S. domestic M&A deals (acquirer <50% target shares before and >50% after acquisition; deal value >$1 million and >10% of acquirer market value), from the SDC U.S. Mergers and Acquisitions database, with acquirer financial data in COMPUSTAT, stock returns in CRSP (≥100 days before announcement), and matching equity lending-supply data in Markit; filters follow Masulis, Wang, and Xie (2007) and Chen et al. (2015)

data_sources.name: Center for Research in Security Prices (CRSP)
Kenneth R. French data library (Fama-French five-industry classification)

controls.name: AcqFixedAsset (ratio of property, plant, and equipment to sales)
two-digit industry dummies and year dummies

analyses.label: Online Appendix Table 2 (Eq. 2 & 3) - Likelihood of Being an Acquiring Firm (propensity score matching + probit)
analyses.sample: nearest-neighbor propensity-score-matched sample of 882 observations (441 unique treated-control pairs)

analyses.label: [withheld: wording matches the source]
